nyc_found: nyc.gov/dep: "We maintain over 6,800 miles of in-city water mains, 109,000 fire hydrants, 148,000 catch basins, and 7,500 miles of in-city sewers."
match_found: London Fire Brigade: "There are over 115,000 fire hydrants in London we inspect them every 4 years."
finding: Both figures check out as quoted and the ratio is correct. Neither source carries a publication date, so currency can't be verified beyond what's live on the page now; the shown caveat about four water companies versus one utility, and both figures being round numbers, is accurate.

nyc_found: nyc.gov DOT bike stats: "1,550 lane miles; North America's largest bicycle network"
match_found: USGS Colorado River Basin page: "The Colorado River is about 1,450 miles long, with headwaters in Colorado and Wyoming..."
finding: Both figures check out as quoted and the ratio is correct. The Colorado River figure is itself an "about" approximation from USGS, not a precise measurement, which the sentence doesn't flag, but the shown caveat about lane miles counting each direction separately covers the more serious apples-to-oranges problem.

nyc_found: Census ACS 2024 1-year (place:51000, state:36): New York city, New York, B25001_001E (housing units) = 3,737,632
match_found: Census ACS 2024 1-year (state:51): Virginia, B25001_001E = 3,746,211
finding: Both figures and the ratio check out exactly. The match_url actually pulls five states at once (NJ, VA, WA, AZ, MA) rather than Virginia alone, so a reader who clicks it has to find Virginia's row themselves, but the number used is correctly Virginia's. 2024 is the latest ACS 1-year data available; 2025 estimates are not yet published (confirmed 404 on the Census API).

nyc_found: Cushman & Wakefield Manhattan Office MarketBeat Q1 2026, market statistics table: "MANHATTAN TOTALS" inventory = 416,146,760 SF
match_found: Lincoln Property/LPC Washington DC Office Market Report Q1 2026: "The Washington, D.C. Metropolitan commercial real estate market is comprised of approximately 428.2 million square feet of rentable office space located in the District of Columbia, Northern Virginia, and Suburban Maryland."
finding: Both figures check out exactly as stated (not sums researchers built themselves) and both reports are current, Q1 2026. The shown caveat about two brokerages and two inventory definitions is apt and sufficient.

nyc_found: nyc.gov/dep: "We maintain over 6,800 miles of in-city water mains..."
match_found: LADWP 2024-25 Water Infrastructure Plan: "Approximately 6,794 miles of Mainline Pipe, 20 inches or smaller in diameter"
derived: The 6,794 figure used for Los Angeles is only LADWP's distribution mainlines 20 inches or smaller. The same document separately states "Approximately 547 miles of Trunk Line Pipe" (larger than 20 inches), and its own introduction gives the combined total directly: "about 7,341 miles of mainlines and trunk lines." 6,794 + 547 = 7,341, confirming the trunk-line miles are excluded from the figure used.
conflict: Same document, page 2 (intro): LADWP "maintains and operates a vast Water System with about 7,341 miles of mainlines and trunk lines and approximately 300 miles of water conveyance system along the Los Angeles Aqueduct." Using the comparable combined total, the ratio becomes 7,341/6,800 = 1.08, not 0.999 as stated.
finding: The LA figure quietly picks the narrower "mainlines only" number from a source that also states a combined mainlines-plus-trunk-lines total on the very same page, and that combined total is the one comparable to NYC's all-inclusive "in-city water mains" figure. There is no caveat disclosing this, and it isn't a rounding issue: using the document's own total changes the relationship from near-parity to LA having about 8% more miles of main than New York.

nyc_found: Central Park Conservancy: "Central Park is New York City's 843-acre backyard..."
match_found: Bayern Schlösserverwaltung: "With an area of 376 hectares respectively 411 hectares (including the Maximilian Park, Court and Finance Gardens), the English Garden is one of the largest inner-city parks in the world..."
derived: 376 hectares x 2.47105 acres/hectare = 929.15 acres, rounding to the 929 acres used. This correctly uses the core 376-hectare garden figure, not the 411-hectare figure that includes the adjoining Maximilianpark and other gardens.
finding: The hectare-to-acre conversion is done correctly and uses the more comparable of the two figures on the source page (the garden alone, not garden-plus-annexes).

nyc_found: mta.info agency page: "5,800 buses"
match_found: Hong Kong government transport factsheet (data as of end 2024): KMB fleet 3,895; Citybus HK/Kowloon/NT network 1,326; Citybus Airport/North Lantau network 226; Long Win Bus Company 281; New Lantao Bus Company 142.
derived: 3,895 + 1,326 + 226 + 281 + 142 = 5,870, matching the figure used. This is genuinely an undisclosed sum on the government's part, as the shown caveat states — the factsheet lists each franchise separately and never gives a combined fleet total.
finding: The sum is arithmetically correct and the caveat accurately describes it as a derived total. The Hong Kong factsheet's underlying data is dated to end of 2024 (about 21 months old), the most recent version available (last modified September 2025); the NYC page's fleet count carries no date and cites 152 million bus miles for 2023 elsewhere on the same page, so the two figures may not be from precisely the same year, though neither source offers a more current alternative.

nyc_found: mta.info NYCT ridership 2025: "2025 subway ridership increased to 1,282 million, up 7.3% year-over-year..."
match_found: Quadratín México: "El Sistema de Transporte Colectivo (STC) Metro cerró el 2025 con una afluencia histórica de poco más de mil 241 millones viajes" (the Metro closed 2025 with a historic ridership of just over 1.241 billion trips).
finding: Both figures check out as stated and are for the same calendar year, 2025.

nyc_found: mta.info NYCT ridership 2025: "Average weekday ridership grew 7.1% to 4.002 million (73% of 2019 levels)..."
match_found: Census Bureau Vintage 2025 city/town population estimates: Los Angeles population 3,869,089.
finding: Both figures check out as stated. The Census release is the newest vintage available (2025 estimates).

nyc_found: mta.info NYCT ridership 2025: "Bus ridership in 2025 increased by 8.1% year-over-year, rising to 442 million annual rides..."
match_found: World Bank API, SP.POP.TOTL, EUU, 2025: 451,127,411
finding: Both figures check out exactly. The shown caveat correctly flags that NYC Transit's bus figure excludes MTA Bus Company (~120 million more rides), which is the more important asterisk here.

nyc_found: NYC Tourism + Conventions 2025 annual report: "New York City Welcomed 65 Million Visitors in 2025"; "Total visitation grew modestly to 65 million visitors, up 0.7% over 2024."
match_found: Daily Sabah: "Türkiye welcomed record 52.78 million foreign tourists in 2025, up 0.3% year-over-year, while total visitor numbers rose 2.7% to a new all-time high of 63.94 million."
finding: The 63.94 million figure and the ratio are correct, but the cited Daily Sabah article never explains why "total visitors" (63.94M) exceeds "foreign tourists" (52.78M) by about 11.2 million; it doesn't itself support the shown caveat that the gap is Turkish citizens living abroad. That explanation is nonetheless correct as a matter of TurkStat methodology (its Departing Visitors Survey and residence-determination survey separately track foreign nationals versus Turkish-passport holders resident abroad), confirmed independently, just not from the URL given.

nyc_found: NYC Tourism + Conventions 2025 annual report: "International travel declined slightly due to global challenges, accounting for 12.5 million visitors, down 3.2% from 2024."
match_found: World Bank API, SP.POP.TOTL, BEL, 2024: 11,858,610
finding: Both figures check out exactly, and the ratio is correct. Note the NYC figure is 2025 and the Belgium population is 2024, the latest year the World Bank has posted for Belgium, so this is a one-year lag rather than an error.

nyc_found: Port Authority 2025 Annual Traffic Report, letter from the Aviation Department: "Our airports served 142.7 million passengers across the region last year..." (JFK, Newark, LaGuardia, Stewart, Teterboro).
match_found: Hurriyet Daily News: "Istanbul Airport handled 84 million passengers by year-end..."; "Sabiha Gökçen served 48 million passengers..."

finding: The 142.7 million figure is stated directly by the Port Authority, not a sum built by the researcher, and the 132 million figure for Istanbul is a correct sum of the two airports named in the same article, which never states a combined total. Both parts of the shown caveat are accurate.

nyc_found: nyc.gov TLC: "By law, there are 13,587 yellow taxis in New York City, and each must have a medallion attached to its hood."
match_found: TfL licensing information, week ending 16 August 2026: "Taxi vehicle licences - 13,483, a decrease of 28 on the previous week..."

match_found: Cleanrider.com: "plus de 49 millions de trajets en Vélib enregistrés en 2024" (more than 49 million Vélib' trips recorded in 2024).
finding: Both figures check out as quoted. The shown caveat correctly discloses that the Paris figure is a year behind (2024 vs. 2025); a full-year 2025 Vélib' total may exist by now but wasn't found in this check (velib-metropole.fr's press page returned a 403).

nyc_found: NY DMV live registration data (data.ny.gov, filtered to record_type='VEH', five boroughs, reg_expiration_date >= today): 2,139,362
match_found: FHWA Highway Statistics 2024, Table MV-1, Mississippi "ALL MOTOR VEHICLES" total: 2,214,249

The FHWA table's own column headers show "ALL MOTOR VEHICLES" = Automobiles + Buses + Trucks + Motorcycles, with no trailer category at all, confirming the shown caveat that the federal total includes motorcycles but has no trailer figure to exclude or include.

nyc_found: mta.info agency page: "472 subway stations"
match_found: Xinhua (news.cn), Dec 27 2025: "至此，上海轨道交通全网运营线路共21条，运营总里程达到906公里，车站总数523座" (Shanghai's transit network now has 21 lines, 906 km of total operating mileage, and 523 stations in total).
finding: The 472 and 523 figures both check out. The shown caveat's claim that NYC's 472 stations "sit inside 423 complexes" is a widely repeated and accurate MTA fact, but it is not supported by the cited nyc_url, which states only the 472 figure and never mentions complexes; a citation for the 423 figure is missing.

nyc_found: Central Park Conservancy About page (undated): "an essential space that welcomes over 42 million visitors annually."
match_found: World Bank API, SP.POP.TOTL, all countries, 2024: Canada = 41,262,329
conflict: Central Park Conservancy, via centralpark.news: "Central Park is projected to welcome over 40 million visitors in 2026," a nearly 15% increase from an approximately 35 million baseline in 2019 (35M x 1.15 ≈ 40.25M). A 2011 Central Park Conservancy study put annual visits at 37–38 million.
finding: The "over 42 million" figure on the About page carries no year and appears to be a static number the Conservancy has repeated since at least the mid-2010s, unchanged through a pandemic dip and recovery. The Conservancy's own more recent and specifically dated projection, for 2026, is "over 40 million," about 2 million lower and built up from a stated 2019 baseline. Using that figure instead would make Canada's population (41.26 million) higher than Central Park's visitor count rather than lower, reversing the direction of the claim.

nyc_found: Artdaily, citing the Met: "The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced today that it welcomed over 5.7 million visitors to its two locations—The Met Fifth Avenue and The Met Cloisters—in the fiscal year that ended on June 30, 2025 (FY25)."
match_found: The Art Newspaper, world's 100 most-visited museums 2025: "the Uffizi with 5.3 million over its three interconnected sites in Florence" (Uffizi Gallery, Pitti Palace, Boboli Gardens).
conflict: The Art Newspaper's own 2025 survey, the same article cited for the Uffizi figure, reports the Met's calendar-year 2025 total directly: "the most popular US museum was the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York with almost 6 million visitors to its main building (up 4% on 2024)" and, in a footnote, "The Met (Met Cloisters 281,807; total 6,265,898)."
finding: The two figures used aren't for the same period: the Met's 5.7 million is a July 2024-June 2025 fiscal year total from a Met press release, while the Uffizi's 5.3 million is a January-December 2025 calendar year total from The Art Newspaper's annual survey. That same survey, cited for the Uffizi number, also reports the Met's calendar-2025 total as 6,265,898, a directly comparable figure the researcher didn't use. Swapping it in changes the ratio from 5.3M/5.7M = 0.93 to 5.3M/6.27M = 0.85, a materially bigger gap than the sentence implies, and it comes from the same publisher as the match figure.
